text: — Oh! Bay Ganyo, Christ is risen! Were you at the palace for the breaking of the fast?

"— Who, me? Well, if it's not me, who's it going to be?" Bay Ganyo answers me, and as he twirls his left mustache, he gives me a sly wink, meaning: "As long as there are fools in the world, will your old pal Ganyo miss out on the easy pickings?"
— Well, how did it go? Was it fun?

— Who cares about being cheerful, there was a rich windfall to be had! I got myself all dressed up like... you know... You know, Holy Week, I fasted and fasted, bloating myself with those cursed beans, and sauerkraut juice on top; I was as hungry as a bedbug. On Saturday, I didn't put a crumb in my mouth. And then they went and set the breaking of the fast for two o'clock in the morning... While I stood in church, it felt like three hundred leeches were sucking at my stomach. You spit and spit, and not even a drop of saliva is left. You try to have a smoke—it doesn't work, your mouth tastes bitter... They said "Christ is risen"—it was twelve o'clock, but how can you wait until two! I told my family to go and break their fast by themselves, and I went into "The Red Crayfish." There, my brother, it was full of people like me—top hats, epaulettes, medals. And they too were waiting for two o'clock to strike. I sat down at a long table; I saw a few bachelors breaking their fast. They had that table of theirs laid out with appetizers, suckling pigs, and Varna wine on top—enough to make your stomach weep. Just looking at the skin of the little pig, I almost lost my mind. Well, what of it, I should have asked those bachelors: "What are you eating there, eh! Pig? Bravo! Let me... you know... a little bit of the skin..."—and the people would have given me some. But no. I've been shy since I was little... (Give me your cigarette case, you smoke good tobacco, Ivanov's is no good at all, it smells like makhorka...) Those bachelors started smacking their lips, it made me angry just to watch them, so I turned my eyes the other way. I thought to spit, but where was the saliva! My intestines were stuck together. I thought about ordering a beer, but then I changed my mind. Is this why I starved myself for, as they say, two days... I supposedly turned away so as not to look at them, but they, as if on purpose, devil take them, kept chewing and kept praising the pig. I felt like, you know, getting up and snatching that cursed pig right out of their mouths... If only I could lean forward, to press my stomach like that—you don't feel the hunger so much then, but I couldn't lean forward. My tailcoat was tight, it would have split down the back. Oh, to hell with it! And the collar was starched so stiffly that it started scraping my neck like a saw... My eyes went dark. I left the Crayfish and headed toward the palace. It’s not proper to go in early. I have a guard friend, a good friend at that, even a bit of a relative if you must know, but it never quite works out. And even if you go in early, it’s all the same, they won't set the table for you right away. I circled and circled around the gates until my legs ached. Finally, at one point, *drrr*... a carriage, a little later *drrr*... another carriage. They entered the palace, thank God! I twisted my mustache a bit, cleared my throat, and followed after them. I went inside, saw the guards, the convoy, already lined up. A clean-shaven boy rushed to take off my overcoat; I grumbled at him: "Excuse me, sir, mind your own business," and I didn't let him undress me. He got embarrassed and went to undress others. How could I let him undress me, brother? The sleeves of my coat, or rather not the sleeves, but the lining inside was all torn like... you know. Anyway. I went upstairs, but before I went up, I cast an eye into the lower rooms—the tables were set, a clean job. A crowd gathered. We waited here a bit too, and then the Prince and Princess came out. This time, in the Christian way, they were truly the host and hostess. They gave each of us an egg...
— Did you kiss the hand again?

— Well, of course... Why, for a feast like that, I would kiss even a hundred hands. Anyway. That ordeal passed too, and when we rushed, my brother, down the stairs... Believe it or not, I was leaping over three steps at a time, I almost crashed into the mirror, but I didn't let anyone get ahead of me. I grabbed the caviar, and when I dug in with the spoon, if it was less than half a kilo—may it be a sin on my soul. That fish mayonnaise, those appetizers, I don't know their names, and when that mouth of mine gaped open... Don't even ask!... I ate and ate, I stuffed myself... and to this day I wonder how my stomach didn't burst. And the drinking... When I left, how I left—kill me, I don't remember... Ugh!... My head still aches from that cursed champagne... And never mind that, but then I went and stuffed my pockets with pastries, and they were soft, devil take them, and they got all smeared inside my pocket... Well, goodbye then.
